basics.name: Omar El Bachyr
basics.label: PhD Researcher
basics.summary: PhD Researcher at the University of Luxembourg, working on information retrieval, multimodal retrieval, visually rich documents, retrieval-augmented generation, and multilingual information retrieval.

work.name: University of Luxembourg
work.summary: Research in the Trustworthy Software (TruX) group at the Interdisciplinary Centre for Security, Reliability and Trust (SnT).
highlights: Information retrieval and retrieval-augmented generation over visually rich documents.

publications.name: RAGit: Turning Document Preprocessing into an Experimental Variable for RAG
publications.publisher: 33rd Asia-Pacific Software Engineering Conference (APSEC), Tool Demonstration Track (accepted, forthcoming)
publications.summary: RAGit is an open-source workbench for comparing document preprocessing choices in retrieval-augmented generation. Configurable parsing, chunking, indexing, retrieval, and evaluation stages support controlled experiments, reusable artifacts, and a shared page-level evaluation across different retrieval units.

publications.name: LëtzCross: A Cross-Lingual Page-Level Benchmark for Multimodal Retrieval over Luxembourgish Documents
publications.publisher: International Conference on Language Technologies for Low-resource Languages (LaTeLL 2026, accepted)
publications.summary: LëtzCross evaluates cross-lingual retrieval over Luxembourgish PDF pages using queries in English, French, German, and Luxembourgish. The benchmark combines textual and visual questions to compare text-only and page-image retrievers, and investigates how single-language and multilingual fine-tuning transfer across query languages.

publications.name: Empirical Evaluation of PDF Parsing and Chunking for Financial Question Answering with RAG
publications.publisher: Proceedings of the IEEE/ACM 48th International Conference on Software Engineering: Software Engineering in Practice
publications.summary: This study examines how PDF parsing and chunking choices affect retrieval-augmented question answering over financial documents. Experiments on two benchmarks, including the newly introduced TableQuest dataset, compare parsers, chunking strategies, and overlap settings to guide the design of document-processing pipelines.

publications.name: M-CATNAT: A Multimodal dataset to analyze French tweets during natural disasters
publications.publisher: Proceedings of the International ISCRAM Conference
publications.summary: M-CATNAT introduces a French-language dataset for multimodal analysis of natural-disaster tweets. Its annotation approach treats tweet text, images, and their combination separately, extending crisis-management resources beyond English and supporting automated analysis of social media during disasters.
